medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 recommends ACE‑I as first‑line for hypertension
NICE NG136 recommends CCB as second‑line/add‑on for hypertension

medications.dose: 20 mg PO once daily in the evening
medications.purpose: Lipid lowering for primary CVD prevention (QRISK ≥10%)
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG181 advises statin (≥20 mg atorvastatin) for adults with QRISK ≥10% or ≥1 CVD risk factor

medications.dose: 500 mg PO once daily with evening meal, increase by 500 mg weekly as tolerated to 1000 mg twice daily (max 2 g/day)
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG28 recommends metformin as first‑line for pre‑diabetes/high cardiovascular risk when eGFR ≥30 mL/min/1.73 m²

medications.dose: 0.25 mg subcutaneous weekly for 4 weeks, then titrate to 0.5 mg weekly (can increase to 1 mg if further weight loss needed)
medications.purpose: Weight management and additional glycaemic control in obesity with pre‑diabetes
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG28 (2024 update) recommends GLP‑1 RA for obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m²) with pre‑diabetes or CVD when weight loss is a therapeutic goal

interactions_checked.interaction: Amlodipine can increase atorvastatin plasma concentration (~2‑fold), raising risk of myopathy
interactions_checked.action: Monitor CK and symptoms of myopathy; if CK >4×ULN consider switching to pravastatin or rosuvastatin

contraindications.reason: Contraindicated if eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m² (risk of lactic acidosis)
contraindications.alternative: If eGFR 30‑45 start 500 mg daily; if <30 avoid metformin

contraindications.reason: Contraindicated in active liver disease or ALT >3× ULN
contraindications.alternative: Use pravastatin or rosuvastatin after confirming normal LFTs

contraindications.reason: Contraindicated in personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN 2
contraindications.alternative: Consider Orlistat 120 mg PO three times daily with meals

assumptions_warnings: eGFR not provided – assumed ≥30 mL/min/1.73 m² for metformin initiation; obtain renal function before starting.
Liver function tests not provided – obtain baseline ALT/AST before starting atorvastatin.
Fasting lipid profile and QRISK score not available – QRISK likely ≥10% given metabolic‑syndrome components; statin can be started while awaiting results.
Smoking status, alcohol intake, and allergy history not documented – need to assess before finalising plan.
Urine microscopy shows leukocytes and glucose – possible urinary infection; treat infection before considering SGLT2‑inhibitor.
treatment_summary: Continue ACE‑I and CCB for hypertension, initiate atorvastatin 20 mg daily for primary CVD prevention, start metformin with cautious titration pending renal function, and begin semaglutide for weight loss and glycaemic benefit. Monitor for statin‑CCB interaction, renal and liver function, and CK levels. Provide lifestyle counselling, referral to the NHS Diabetes Prevention Programme, and arrange follow‑up in 4 weeks to review tolerance and lab results.
